thread:
sec-bot: Security alert: new NVIDIA stack CVE posted: CVE-2026-0123 affecting NVIDIA Linux driver userland API and cuDNN NCCL interactions. Vendor advisory: https://nvidia.example/advisory (internal mirror: INFRA-3421). Affects driver versions < 535.86 and cuDNN < 8.10.3.

sam.norman: ack — thanks. Quick triage: is this local privilege escalation or remote?

sec-bot: vendor says local privilege escalation via crafted userland input to driver API; attacker needs local access. Severity: HIGH (CVSS 7.8).

priya.k: this is concerning primarily for our Dedicated and Private on-prem clusters where build machines run as shared users. Hosted API less likely but still possible if a bad container escapes. Need to prioritize driver bump on any host with GPUs.

devon: can we get a short compatibility matrix? Which CUDA/cuDNN/NCCL combos are known-good with driver >=535.86? I worry about breaking runtime for existing models.

priya.k: current stack we use in prod: driver 525.85, CUDA 11.8 for older stacks and CUDA 12.1 for newer. cuDNN 8.8.x on CUDA11 and 8.10.x on CUDA12. NCCL 2.14 -> 2.18. Vendor tested combos that include patched driver: 535.x + CUDA 12.1 + cuDNN 8.10.3 + NCCL 2.18 is green. Older CUDA11 stacks may need validation — vendor suggests 535 driver maintains CUDA11 backwards compatibility but we must run our QA.

lee: propose plan: 1) immediate mitigation: restrict local access (RBAC) to GPU hosts, disable interactive shells for build CI agents that don't need GPU; 2) schedule staged driver upgrade on gpu-staging -> gpu-canary -> gpu-prod; 3) run compatibility validation (short harness).

sam.norman: agree. For RBAC, we can add a group `gpu-admins` and apply sftp-only for CI users. ops-bot, can you open INFRA ticket and set high priority?

ops-bot: Created ticket INFRA-3421-update-drivers-priority-high. Added checklist and assigned to devops/gpu-team. ETA field left blank.

devon: compatibility validation harness (proposal):
```
# smoke test (run on single GPU node)
docker run --gpus all --rm quay.io/redwood/inference:smoke /bin/bash -c "python smoke_infer.py --model redwood-small"
# NCCL ring test
/usr/local/nccl-tests/build/all_reduce_perf -b 8 -e 512M -f 2 -g 1
# cuDNN conv correctness quick test (reference)
python test_cudnn_conv.py --iterations 20
```
We should also run a small multi-node NCCL test on canary.

priya.k: add model-level regression: run 5 prompts from our smoke prompt set for LLM and compare logits/latency within tolerance (we detect significant regresses). Also check GPU metrics: mem, clock, and ECC errors after upgrade.

lee: timeline suggestion: 0-24h mitigation (RBAC + restrict CI), 24-72h deploy to gpu-staging and validate, 72-120h canary on <10% traffic Dedicated, then rollout. If any model regresses, rollback immediately.

sam.norman: who owns the kernel compatibility verification? Some nodes run distro kernel 5.10 and 5.15; driver 535 tested on both but we should validate DKMS and module builds. @devon you have config for kernel matrix, right?

devon: yes — I'll run module build across kernels in our fleet matrix (5.10, 5.15, 6.1) in parallel. Will report build logs in INFRA-3421. Also will run `dkms status` and confirm modules load: `modinfo nvidia` + `nvidia-smi` smoke.

priya.k: from compliance side: audit logging must capture driver package changes and KMS key accesses for any image signing related to driver blobs. Who can update audit rules?

lee: security/audit can add rule to Auditd: watch /lib/modules and package manager logs. I'll coordinate with sec to add KMS access logs to alert pipeline for image signing events.

sam.norman: good — add one-off RBAC change to require `sudo` approvals for GPU hosts. Also update runbooks for incident response: add this CVE to our quick triage checklist.

sec-bot: runbook note added: RBAC -> restrict gpu host shell access, Audit -> watch driver package installs, KMS -> log key unwrap for signing.

devon: risk note: most likely attack requires local user; so main exposure is multi-tenant CI runners and self-hosted dev workstations. Patch priority: high for Dedicated/Private, medium for hosted with ephemeral containers.

priya.k: OK actionable summary: 1) RBAC changes applied within 12h (sam/lee) 2) staging driver upgrade + compatibility tests within 48h (devon) 3) canary rollout within 72-120h (devops) 4) audit & KMS logging rules added (lee/sec) 5) regressions -> rollback + postmortem.

sam.norman: I've volunteered to triage regressions during canary hours. If anything blocks, ping me in #oncall.

ops-bot: Canaries scheduled: gpu-staging 1732180000, gpu-canary 1732200000 (tentative).

lee: last note — make sure to tag any driver kernel modules with package version so our upgrade automation can detect mismatch: `nvidia-driver-535.86-<kernel>` in package metadata.

priya.k: thanks everyone. I'll prepare the audit rule PR and a short compliance summary for SOC.

sam.norman: closing loop — assign post-upgrade verification to qa/gpu and mark INFRA-3421 in JIRA. :thumbsup:

sec-bot: resolved: triage complete, mitigation plan in INFRA-3421, monitoring rules pending.
